Subject: SLO stitching — p95/p99 E2E targets & streaming window (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks for taking time earlier, Liam & Priya — quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on perf gating for a potential migration to Redwood hosted.

High-level notes from the call:
- Customer goal: match or improve incumbent E2E p95/p99 for document parsing API (OCR -> normalize -> LLM) at current traffic volumes and burst patterns.
- Current provider metrics (provided by Orbital): p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 980ms for 1–3k RPS steady; spikes to 6k RPS during morning syncs.
- Streaming requirement: client uses server-sent chunking for long transcripts; want consistent streaming window <= 100ms per chunk.
- Key gating questions: concurrency envelope, end-to-end prefix caching opportunity, and acceptable tail tradeoffs for large documents (>2k tokens).

Immediate asks we agreed on:
1) Orbital to share a representative traffic profile (CSV) and two example long-document traces (timestamps + size).
2) Redwood to run a small hosted probe against a synthetic copy (we'll emulate your envelope) and produce p95/p99 E2E numbers and a short SLO-stitching doc.
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (solutions + infra) to validate streaming window and KV-cache strategy.

I've attached a starting SLO draft (redwood-slo-draft-20270527.pdf) and the HubSpot opp link. Ben / Karthik / Marissa — can you own the probe plan and propose dates?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Thanks Grace — attaching the traffic profile per item (1). A couple clarifications from our infra team: 
- "Spikes" are usually short (30–90s) but can be back-to-back across services (so sustained higher concurrency for ~5–10 minutes).
- We currently batch up to 8 requests server-side before sending to incumbent provider; would like to preserve batching benefits if possible.
- Our p99 incidents are tied to two things: cold KV cache misses and long tail from GPU reloads during quantized model swaps.

Attachments: orbital_traffic_profile.csv

Next steps from our side:
- We're available for a deep-dive on Monday 31 May (10:00–11:00 PT) or Tuesday 1 Jun (14:00–15:00 PT).
- We will also pull a small trace extract (1–2 sample traces) and share by EOD Friday.

—Priya

Thanks Priya — got the traffic CSV. Initial internal notes / plan: 

Plan for hosted probe (action items):
- Karthik: build a synthetic replay harness that replays orbital_traffic_profile.csv into our hosted ingress (will mark as non-prod test project). Focus on matching: RPS distribution, burstiness, and size mix.
- Karthik: instrument to capture end-to-end time broken down into ingress queue -> model latency -> post-processing (normalize) -> network egress.
- Run two probe profiles: (A) baseline with our default quantized model + warm cache; (B) cold-cache + simulated quantized model swap events to proxy incumbent behavior.
- Target deliverables: single-sheet p95/p99 comparison + a short SLO-stitching appendix describing where host-level fallbacks would trigger.

Open technical questions for Orbital:
- Can you share a short list of your batch semantics? (server-side batch size and max latency tolerated per batch)
- What is the max acceptable degradation for p99 during a 5–10 minute burst window (e.g., 1.5x, 2x)? We should lock this for run acceptance.

Proposed schedule:
- Probe run: Fri 28 May -> results by EOD Mon 31 May.
- Deep-dive: Monday 31 May 10:00 PT (confirm) — Karthik to present instrumentation.

I'll prepare the runbook and attach the probe script after it's checked in.

—Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Perfect — locking Monday 31 May 10:00–11:00 PT for the deep-dive. Agenda: 1) Karthik walkthrough of probe harness + instrumentation, 2) runbook for hosted probe execution, 3) acceptance criteria (p95/p99 & streaming chunk window), 4) timeline for small PoC.

Acceptance criteria (proposal — please confirm):
- p95 E2E <= 220ms for the nominal envelope (matches current baseline or better).
- p99 E2E <= 1.2s during steady-state; during 5–10 minute burst windows, p99 may be allowed up to 2.0s if documented and agreed.
- Streaming chunk latency <= 100ms (for chunks <= 256 tokens) with <2% chunk-drop events.
- Evidence: the probe must include an annotated waterfall (ingress/model/postproc) for at least 10k requests to validate tail sources.

If Orbital is aligned, Ben/Karthik will execute the probe Friday and circulate results on Monday morning; we'll use the deep-dive to iterate on SLO wording and the draft doc.

Thanks — looking forward.
Grace
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
